question_text: What is referred to as a satellite chromosome?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Labelled sketch
steps.why: The sketch is the fastest way to show the three parts in the right order down the chromosome: satellite at the top, then the secondary constriction, then the centromere.
common_mistakes: Drawing the satellite below the centromere. It lies on the short arm, beyond the secondary constriction.
Leaving the labels off. The three labels are what is marked.
steps.memory_tip: Read the sketch downwards: satellite, secondary constriction, centromere.

steps.label: Definition

lines.text: SAT chromosome = one that carries a satellite

lines: The centromere is the primary constriction.
A few chromosomes have a second narrow region
as well, called the secondary constriction.
The short rounded piece lying beyond the
steps.why: A satellite can only be defined once the secondary constriction is defined, because the satellite is the piece that lies beyond it.
common_mistakes: Calling the centromere the secondary constriction. The centromere is the primary one.
Writing that every chromosome has a satellite. Only a few do.
steps.memory_tip: Primary constriction = centromere. Secondary constriction = the one that cuts off the satellite.
steps.margin_note: Name both constrictions before you define the satellite.

insider_note: Two marks, and one of them is for showing where the satellite sits — a labelled sketch answers this faster than a paragraph.
